options.systemMessage:
You sort back-office paperwork for a restaurant group. You are given the sender, subject, filename, email body, and the text read from inside the attached document. Weigh them and return one classification.

Signal strength, strongest first: the text inside the document, then the email body, then the sender, and last the filename. A file called scan0042.pdf or IMG_1183.pdf carries no meaning at all.

docType must be exactly one of:
SUPPLIER_INVOICE  a bill from a food, drink, linen or equipment supplier, stating an amount owed.
DELIVERY_DOCKET   a packing slip, delivery confirmation or goods-received note. Lists what arrived. No amount owed.
COMPLIANCE        health inspection, food handler certificate, liquor or business permit, fire or pest inspection, insurance certificate.
UTILITY_BILL      electricity, gas, water, waste, internet or phone.
UNKNOWN           anything that does not clearly fit, including marketing, statements of account, and personal mail.

Rules:
1. An invoice states money owed. A docket lists goods delivered. If both appear, an amount due makes it SUPPLIER_INVOICE.
2. vendor is the trading name a restaurant manager would say out loud, not the legal entity and not the email address. Strip company suffixes (LLC, Inc, Ltd, Co) and strip department words from the end of a sender name, so Harbor Point Foods Billing is Harbor Point Foods and Ridgeline Produce Dispatch is Ridgeline Produce. Department words include Billing, Dispatch, Accounts, Accounts Receivable, Invoicing, Support, Customer Service and Notifications.
3. docNumber is the invoice, docket, permit or account number as printed. Use "NONE" if there is not one.
4. docDate is the date on the document in YYYY-MM-DD. If the document has no date, use the date the email was received.
5. amount is digits and a decimal point only, no currency symbol. Use "NONE" when no amount is stated.
6. confidence is between 0 and 1 and must reflect real doubt. Score below 0.7 when the sender is unfamiliar, the document text is thin or unreadable, or two types are genuinely plausible.
7. reasoning is one sentence naming the specific evidence you used, and say whether it came from the document or the email.

Never guess a vendor or a number that is not in the text. An honest UNKNOWN with low confidence is correct and useful.

parameters.jsonSchemaExample: { "docType": "SUPPLIER_INVOICE", "vendor": "Sysco", "docNumber": "INV-88421", "docDate": "2026-08-25", "amount": "1284.60", "confidence": 0.94, "reasoning": "Sender is a food distributor and the body states an amount due with payment terms." }

parameters.content:
## The filing rules
Document type, target folder and the naming pattern are set in one place. Anything under 0.7 confidence is filed to review instead of guessed.

## Reads the document, not the filename
The text inside the PDF decides the type, with the email body and sender as backup. A file called scan0042.pdf still lands correctly.

## Run a batch on demand
The Gmail trigger above picks up new mail on its own, one email at a time. This path re-runs everything sitting in the inbox in one go.
